title: I made an SDK for NPCs that remember what you did and act on it. The part that decides is a small trained model, not an LLM. Free for a week.
author: tyn_21
selftext:
You write three things for a character: who he is, what he can do, what he must never do. Then he runs on his own.

Every NPC system makes you pick. Script it and it's fast but dead. Use an LLM and it's alive but slow, expensive, and it'll break character the moment a player pushes it. I built a third option: a trained model under half a megabyte, built with a research technique I developed, that decides what a character does, runs in your build offline, and physically can't break the rules you wrote for it.

• **What picks** is a trained model under half a megabyte, running in your build. What she perceives plus her memory plus her role goes in, a probability on every action she could take comes out. No prompt, no network on the frame, a few milliseconds, nothing per decision.  
• **Two things aren't local**, so you know going in. Multi-step planning is one small call to my server; if it's down, characters keep reacting and remembering, they just stop making new long plans and it still doesn’t use an llm for the planning.  
• **Dialogue is optional** and you can use a free local LLM, and it never decides what a character does.  
• **Every decision writes a receipt** you can read when something looks wrong.  
• **Need a behaviour a character doesn't have in our current brain?** Ask for it and it comes back trained and tested. You never touch machine learning.  
• **pip install**, websocket into any engine, MCP server if your coding agent is doing the wiring.  
• **Seven days free**, no card, then $20/mo.
